- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.3) and prices are rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast decline, it often overcorrects; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% in next period.  
- If true outcome consistently lags model by 1–3 days, apply a 1–2% downward bias to forecast for the following 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.6) and model is trending upward, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid mean reversion overreaction.  
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome by 2–4% over 3–5 days, apply a 1–2% downward correction to next forecast.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish, model often overestimates; apply 1–3% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence bias.
